scope: Seven core knowls and their 22 morphism-space records; all 26 sporadic group definitions and the Leech-lattice prerequisite. This is targeted mathematical review, not a full-source or dependency certification.
hash_policy: source_sha256 is SHA-256 of the current complete local file when this evidence record was written. The targeted claims identify what was reviewed; these hashes do not expand the pass to later interlinks, metadata or other untargeted prose.

direct_tests.method: Parsed the seven core files and their existing direct wiki-link targets, rendered each core and all its sections, and checked for actual KaTeX/math-render error markers.
direct_tests.historical_note: At execution time, the only unresolved local targets were three not-yet-generated lane indexes and two pending Lie-type construction pages. This records the earlier scoped check, not a new final-site link audit.
direct_tests.program:
from pathlib import Path
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, 'packages/compiler')
import knowl_compile as c
root = Path('../knowlpedia-content')
paths = [root / line for line in (root / 'reviews/finite-groups/core-paths.txt').read_text().splitlines() if line.strip()]
knowls = [c.parse_single_file(p) for p in paths]
registry = {k.id: k for k in knowls}
pending = []
for k in knowls:
    for match in c.WIKILINK_RE.finditer(k.core_markdown + '\n' + '\n'.join(s.get('markdown', '') for s in k.sections)):
        target = match.group(1).split('#')[0]
        p = root / 'content' / f'{target}.knowl.md'
        if p.exists() and target not in registry:
            registry[target] = c.parse_single_file(p)
        elif not p.exists():
            pending.append(target)
for k in knowls:
    html = c.render_knowl_core(k, registry) + ''.join(c.render_section(s, registry) for s in k.sections)
    print(k.id, 'render_error', bool('katex-error' in html or 'math-render-error' in html))
print('Pending local targets:', sorted(set(pending)))

direct_tests.method: Standard-library Python parsed cycles from the displayed definitions, generated each seed-block orbit, then counted all t-subsets and asserted count one for every such subset.
direct_tests.limitations: Verifies the displayed Steiner block orbits only; does not independently establish group order or simplicity.

data_reviews.evidence: Read the category and morphism records against the seven core pages. Checked cyclic Hom/End/Aut formulas and underlying-set counts; finite-group and abelian-group full-subcategory views retain the same group homomorphisms. Empty conditions on the generic cyclic records are conditional on the fg-cyclic-n object retaining n>=1. No inference of Hom from End or of uncatalogued maps was introduced.
data_reviews.limitations: No independent exhaustive Hom enumeration was performed. This supplemental data review is not a claim to have re-reviewed unrelated catalogue shards.

limitations: Only the targeted claims are certified as reviewed. The later Mathieu-point-stabilizer and Baby-Monster-subgroup relationship knowls are outside these two passes.

entries.targeted_claims: The full subcategory of groups on finite objects retains all group homomorphisms.
entries.evidence: Checked directly that only objects are restricted: identities and composition remain group homomorphisms, and no new regularity or homomorphism condition is introduced.

entries.targeted_claims: Full subcategory on nontrivial finite simple groups; trivial morphisms remain allowed.
entries.evidence: Checked the nontrivial simple-group convention and full-subcategory meaning. A homomorphism from a simple group has kernel either the whole source or the identity subgroup; this does not justify deleting trivial maps from the category.

entries.targeted_claims: Family versus individual-group display semantics; exceptional Lie type versus sporadic groups; cluster labels versus subgroup claims.
entries.evidence: Read the overview for ambiguous mathematical claims. Family tiles do not claim one finite order, composition factors do not determine every finite group, and display clusters do not assert direct embeddings.
limitations: Navigation links and wording added after the original pass are outside this targeted mathematical review.

entries.targeted_claims: Cyclic Hom count, endomorphism ring, automorphism units, order-one boundary case, and underlying-set map counts.
entries.evidence: Derived f([k])=[ka] from the image of a generator. Well-definedness is n dividing ma, giving gcd(m,n) possible images. Addition of homomorphisms is residue addition and composition is residue multiplication; automorphisms are units. Checked the n=1 case using the one-element ring and its one-element unit group. Independently checked that arbitrary set maps C_m to C_n number n^m, endomaps number n^n, and set automorphisms number n!. Full group and abelian-group subcategories retain the same homomorphisms.
limitations: This was symbolic reasoning, not exhaustive enumeration over parameter values.

entries.targeted_claims: End(G) is the disjoint union of the trivial endomorphism and Aut(G) for nontrivial finite simple G.
entries.evidence: Checked normality of the kernel, the two kernel cases, injective-to-surjective implication for a self-map of a finite set, and product preservation by the inverse of a bijective homomorphism. Nontriviality makes the zero map distinct from every automorphism.

entries.targeted_claims: Exact Y555 Coxeter quotient and extraction of one Monster by C_G(a)/<a>.
entries.evidence: Checked all sixteen vertices, the three length-five arms, the adjacency/nonadjacency relations, and the length-nine spider word raised to the tenth power against Allcock section 2. Independently checked the centralizer deduction: connected odd Coxeter edges identify all involution generators in the abelianization; every relator has even length, so the abelianization is C2. Under the cited bimonster theorem the perfect base H x H is the commutator subgroup, so a lies outside it. An outside involution has form (h,h^-1)tau and is conjugate to tau. Its centralizer is diag(H) x <tau>, and quotienting the central involution gives H.
